profile.summary: An endemic tufted sedge of freshwater wetlands, streambanks, lake margins and damp forest. Its long pale green leaves surround stems carrying several crowded flowering spikes.
profile.lookFor: Look for long folded leaves and several short female spikes clustered close to the base of a terminal male spike. Confirm flowering material before distinguishing similar sedges.
profile.nameNote: NZPCN recognises Carex maorica as a distinct species and does not list Carex secta as its synonym. WRT nursery identity remains unresolved; these species-specific references do not resolve which stock a historic record represented. Keep SP-015 and SP-016 separate. No verified Māori vernacular name was found; Māori sedge is the documented common name.

profile.summary: An endemic forest tree with a marked change between its wiry, small-leaved juvenile form and broader adult foliage. Small red fruits develop along the branches.
profile.lookFor: Young plants have slender interlacing twigs and tiny irregularly lobed leaves. Adult leaves are small and oval with shallow teeth and visible veins; fruit is red.
profile.nameNote: The database spelling Streblus heterophyllus is retained. NZPCN currently accepts Paratrophis microphylla and explicitly lists Streblus heterophyllus as a synonym. These source names refer to this taxon, not a merged database record.

profile.summary: An endemic low shrub of upland grassland and rocky places. It forms an intricate network of short branches with tiny glossy leaves and orange to reddish fruit.
profile.lookFor: Look for branches that spread in a flattened pattern, with many short side twigs at near-right angles. Small pointed leaves occur in pairs or tight clusters; fine hairs are present on the young twigs.
profile.nameNote: No common or Māori name was documented in the checked NZPCN species account. The database scientific name is retained.

profile.summary: A native creeping shrub that spreads by wiry stems rooting at their nodes. Its mats carry very small round or oval leaves; the fruit has a black seed surrounded by fleshy white flower parts.
profile.lookFor: Look for a close ground-covering mat of thin reddish-brown stems and tiny rounded leaves. Pale star-like flowers occur in leaf axils; white fleshy fruit surrounds a dark triangular centre.
profile.nameNote: Pōhuehue is a shared Māori name used for more than one Muehlenbeckia species. Creeping pōhuehue and the scientific name distinguish this low-growing species.

profile.summary: An endemic low, spreading whipcord hebe of Otago and Southland mountain grassland and scrub. Its narrow green branchlets carry closely pressed scale leaves, with small groups of white flowers at the tips.
profile.lookFor: Look for upright or ascending cord-like shoots with overlapping rounded green scales and visible joints between them. Similar whipcord hebes need careful comparison of scales, branchlets and flowers.
profile.nameNote: Whipcord hebe is a shared common name for several species. NZPCN accepts Veronica propinqua and lists Hebe propinqua as a synonym. No Māori name was documented in the checked species account.
